object_description: rectangular two-storey building on a raised plinth wrapped as a shell around a central sports hall
geometry_property: hall at the centre with functions as a shell around it
design_condition: a rectangular volume on a raised plinth answers the heterogeneous avenue with a disciplined geometry, taking the lowered triple sports hall as the core around which all other functions are wrapped

positive: The design responds to the heterogeneous urban situation with a simple and disciplined structure
Precise positioning, clear geometry and disciplined urban design create a strongly organising element
Setting the volume on a one-metre plinth gives it its own base towards the avenue
The uniform facade has an accentuated horizontal structure and a powerful vertical rhythm from the regular columns
The strict facade concept gives the building strong conciseness and a certain serenity as an independent volume
It does not compete directly with the large neighbouring hall buildings
The second tree row supplements the avenue and creates an atmospheric spatial filter
The wide-span spatial structure illuminates the hall and accommodates additional spatial requirements
The daylight supply to the rooms in the bridges is intensive
Sun and glare protection measures are explained in detail
The concept enables compactness and a consistent emphasis on horizontality
The raised plinth acts as an arrival platform and gives the building its own address in a disparate environment
The gallery encompassing the hall provides clear access to all spatial units
The central hall makes it easy to find your way around on the main floor
The organisation of the basement is clear and functional
The spatial presence of the hall creates an exceptional spatial experience for all functional areas
The volume is the smallest in floor area and can be described as compact
The load-bearing structure is easy to read and the costs are within the normal range
Clarity and conciseness give the structure a strong identity and create order in a heterogeneous environment
negative: The catering area cannot be separated from the circulation areas
Connecting the vertical accesses to the central entrance involves considerable distances and spatial bottlenecks
The terrace doubling as cafeteria outdoor area could lead to conflicts of use
The western alley for deliveries and bicycles is significantly restricted between the existing trees
Bicycle parking only behind the building will lead to bikes being parked wildly at the main entrance
The terrace is the only usable outdoor space and makes obstacle-free access impossible
The lack of views from the bridge rooms and the mutual overlooking are considered problematic
The central hall causes very long and not particularly attractive routes
There is no natural centre for informal meetings, as the centre is always occupied by the hall
The room depth along the hall is unsuitable for a library and a well-proportioned cafeteria
The raised floor level creates an undesirable level difference for deliveries
The kitchen area is complicated with internal stairs, lift and corridors
Patient flow is suboptimal due to long distances and branch corridors
Office areas partly lit through the hall skylights create an undesirable internal facade and shading conflicts
The lighting and shading systems are extremely complicated and costly to maintain
Views into the hall from all sides are perceived as a disruptive factor and the side entrances are unattractive
Car parking behind the building has an impractical narrow driveway far from the disabled access
Delivery via the neighbouring property is not possible
Expensive fire-resistant glazing and large roof glazing make the project significantly more expensive
The central hall creates constraints that restrict functions and processes
